## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to design a pluggable, runtime-extensible policy system for high-signal services like API gateways, focusing on lifecycle, concurrency, and hot-reload.

## Key Concepts
- Strategy pattern for interchangeable policies
- Runtime registry for dynamic policy discovery
- Thread-safety and hot-reload considerations

## Code Example
```typescript
interface RequestContext { route: string; user: User; metadata: any }
interface PolicyDecision { allow: boolean; reason?: string; quotas?: any }
interface Policy { apply(ctx: RequestContext): PolicyDecision }
class PolicyFactory { create(config: any): Policy }
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you version policies and rollback safely?
- How would you isolate policies across tenants and credentials?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to extend behavior without touching core dispatch logic; demonstrates the Command pattern with a runtime registry.

## Key Concepts
- Command pattern
- Registry-based extensibility
- Safe, non-invasive extension

## Code Example
```javascript
interface Command { execute(args: string[]): void; }
class Registry { private map = new Map<string, Command>(); register(name: string, c: Command) { this.map.set(name, c); } get(name: string): Command | undefined { return this.map.get(name); } }
class Router { constructor(private registry: Registry) {} route(argv: string[]) { const cmd = argv[0]; const command = this.registry.get(cmd); if (command) command.execute(argv.slice(1)); else throw new Error('Unknown command'); } }
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you handle asynchronous commands? 
- How would you ensure thread-safety in a multi-process CLI?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Dynamic circuit-breaking with runtime rule extension is common in large-scale systems but hard to implement safely. This tests how a candidate balances performance, correctness, and distribution.

## Key Concepts
- Circuit-breaker state per endpoint
- Runtime registries and factories
- Distributed state and synchronization
- Testing concurrent trips and race conditions

## Code Example
```javascript
```javascript
interface CircuitBreakerRule {
  name: string
  shouldTrip(ctx: any): boolean
  onStateChange?(ctx: any): void
}
type RuleFactory = () => CircuitBreakerRule
class Registry {
  private map = new Map()
  register(name, factory){ this.map.set(name, factory) }
  create(name){ const f = this.map.get(name); return f ? f() : null }
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you persist circuit-breaker state across a cluster?
- How would you test time-based thresholds and backoff without slowing tests?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests runtime extensibility, registry design, non-blocking fan-out, and routing policy decisions. Also evaluates trade-offs between Strategy and Chain in a pluggable auditing pipeline.

## Key Concepts
- Runtime plugin registry and factories
- Non-blocking, bounded concurrency routing
- Per-event routing rules and backpressure handling
- Strategy vs Chain trade-offs in routing

## Code Example
```typescript
interface Event { source: string; severity: 'info'|'warning'|'error'; category: string; payload: any }
interface Auditor { log(event: Event): Promise<void> }
type AuditorFactory = () => Auditor
class AuditorRegistry { register(name: string, f: AuditorFactory); create(name: string): Auditor }
class Router { constructor(private reg: AuditorRegistry, private rules: Array<(e:Event)=>boolean>); route(e:Event): Promise<void> }
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test the registry and routing guarantees?
- What metrics would you collect for backpressure and throughput?

questions.explanation:
Why This Is Asked

Tests ability to design a runtime-extensible policy system with hot-reload and safe concurrent access in a high-throughput gateway. It probes how policies are composed per-route, how to avoid downtime during updates, and how to version or rollback policies.

Key Concepts

- Strategy/Policy pattern
- Registry and dynamic module loading
- Atomic swaps and concurrency control
- Per-route pipelines and cache invalidation

Code Example

```javascript
// Implementation sketch
export interface Policy {
  apply(req, ctx, next: () => Promise<void>): Promise<void>
}
export class PolicyRegistry {
  get(name: string): () => Policy
}
```

Follow-up Questions

- How would you test hot-reload safety and latency?
- How would you version policies and roll back on failure?
